messages.content: You are a bounded code reviewer. Return only: verdict, concrete counterexample if any, and the smallest safe dependency. Do not propose implementation beyond the stated ticket boundaries.

Review this FG-177 isolation decision. Facts from the code: StepValueUse.find calls callAnswers with only (stepName, literalReturnStdoutTrue, literalReturnStatusTrue), before execution. WalkerRules.returnContract has the same three inputs. normaliseHostedCall and hostedSignatureError run later, when the hosted call is reached. Ten vocabulary steps have no named-key schema; their fallback checks only excess positional arity. The pinned Jenkins 2.568.1 probe measured echo(message:'x', unknown:true), unstable(message:'x', unknown:true), and unstash(name:'x', unknown:true) throwing constructor-map coercion failures. Fogell currently promotes the required key, leaves the unknown key unchecked, dispatches while ignoring it, and its result slot remains VNull. Proposed null slice would mark those step names GenuineNull and make StepValueUse stop refusing their values. Decision: do not implement that return-only slice; require the per-step call descriptor/validator first. A positional-only allowlist in StepValueUse is rejected because it duplicates call schema. Is this no-go justified, or can the null slice remain sound without implementing/duplicating call schema?
